newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan seen buying 70,000T corn, 38,000T soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan seen buying 70,000T corn, 38,000T soybeans.

text.p: Taiwan traders said on Monday they expect to see perhaps two tenders this week for up to 70,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 38,000 tonnes of soybeans.

The traders, in general, considered the latest U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) crop estimates issued on Friday to be a bullish signal, but expect only a short-term boost to the U.S. futures market.
"The USDA report is bullish, but the futures market should quiet down in a few days," one said.

The traders said the latest USDA supply and demand estimates could delay Taiwan's tender schedule or force traders to buy on a basis price (at premiums to Chicago futures contracts), locking in shipping, storage and other overhead costs while waiting for futures prices to find their level.
Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group said it would place a tender for a 54,000-tonne corn shipment, but that it was likely to buy on a basis price.
"We are still planning to tender (for corn) soon, but this likely will be on basis price," a buyer at Members Feed Industry Group said without giving a firm date.
The shipment's pricing on the futures market could be postponed for weeks, the buyer added.
Hui Shung Group may place a tender for a combined shipment totalling 54,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and soybeans. The shipment would be slated for late March delivery, traders said.
The Taiwan Flour Mills Association was likely to remain out of the international wheat market this week, association official Lu Wei-chih said.
Local flour prices listed on Monday ranged between T$14.55 to T$15.68 a kg for Taipei delivery, unchanged from a week earlier.
Taiwan's domestic soymeal price for Taipei delivery was indicated at between T$9.40 to T$9.60 a kg, down from T$9.55 to T$9.75 a week earlier.
Corn powder was quoted at T$6.75 a kg for Taipei delivery, down from T$6.8 to T$85 the previous week.

The grain freight rate from the U.S. Pacific Northwest to Taiwan was quoted at about US$12.50 a tonne and from the Gulf of Mexico in range of between $22.50 and $23.00 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.
